identity.name: Venetian Dalmatia
alt_names: Provveditore generale in Dalmazia e Albania

land.text: Zadar and its neighbourhood, bought with Ladislaus's rights in 1409

predecessors.note: The page does not name which cities Venice held in 1409-1419. Kotor and Budva came in 1420 (Albania Veneta page).

land.text: "Venetian Istria, Venetian Dalmatia and the Bay of Kotor region were turned over to the Habsburg emperor" by the Treaty of Campo Formio, 17 October 1797

successors.note: Dalmatia passed to the Kingdom of Italy in 1805, to the Illyrian Provinces in 1809 and to the Austrian Empire in 1815, when the Kingdom of Dalmatia was created (Venetian Dalmatia page).

capitals.name: Zadar (Zara)
capitals.note: Seat of the Provveditore Generale, "usually based in Zadar" (Venetian Dalmatia page); the page dates neither the office nor the seat.

correction.text: Zadar and its neighbourhood, bought with Ladislaus's rights in 1409, with the islands of Rab, Hvar and Korčula, which the Stato da Màr page dates "1409–1797"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria's Republic of Venice row does not hold Dalmatia. The page names no city Venice held before 1420, so the 40 km circle round Zadar is the researcher's reading. The islands are circles round Rab (14.78 E, 44.77 N), Hvar and Korčula (Stato da Màr page: Rab "1409–1797", Hvar "1331–1358 and 1409–1797", Korčula "1255–1358 and 1409–1797"). [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: islands added]

correction.text: the Dalmatian coastal cities, "fully incorporated into the Stato da Màr" in 1420 except Ragusa, with the Kotor area and Budva and the islands: Rab, Hvar, Korčula (1409), Pag and Brač (1420) and Cres with Lošinj ("15C–1797", bridged to 1420)

keyframe_review.note: Venetian Dalmatia: Venice "held the coastal cities by 1420, except Ragusa"; Albania Veneta: "The Kotor-area territories and Budva are dated from [1420]". Stato da Màr: Pag "1420–1797 except brief Ottoman occupation during the Cretan War (1645–1669)", Brač "1268–1358 and 1420–1797", Cres and Lošinj "15C–1797 except brief Ottoman occupation of Cres during the Cretan War" (the century is all the page gives, so 1420 is a bridge at confidence 1 for Cres). The circles round Zadar, Šibenik and Split are the researcher's reading of a "very narrow coastal land strip"; the page gives no area. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: islands added, shape split at 1480 for Krk]

correction.text: the same coast and islands with Krk (Veglia), which the Stato da Màr page dates "1480–1797 except brief Ottoman occupation during the Cretan War (1645–1669)"

keyframe_review.note: Stato da Màr: Krk "1480–1797" with a brief Ottoman occupation in the Cretan War. The page does not name the previous holder. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: new keyframe]

correction.text: the strip without Novigrad and without Krk, Pag and Cres, which "In 1646 the Ottomans attacked and took"

keyframe_review.note: Venetian Dalmatia: "In 1646 the Ottomans attacked and took Krk, Pag, Cres, and Novigrad" (Novigrad "surrendered on 4 July, after only two days of bombardment"); Stato da Màr confirms a "brief Ottoman occupation" of Krk, Pag and Cres during the Cretan War. The Novigrad circle (15.52 E, 44.19 N, 8 km) and the three islands are removed for 1646 only. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: new keyframe, the loss is now drawn]

correction.text: the strip again with Novigrad (retaken by Leonardo Foscolo "the following year") and, bridged, the three islands

keyframe_review.note: Venetian Dalmatia: "The following year, the Venetian commander Leonardo Foscolo retook Novigrad". The page is silent on when Krk, Pag and Cres came back (Stato da Màr: "brief Ottoman occupation"), so their return in 1647 is a bridge at confidence 1. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: new keyframe]

correction.text: after the Candia War, when "Venice's territory had roughly tripled"

keyframe_review.note: Venetian Dalmatia: the 1669 peace, "after which Venice's territory had roughly tripled". The wider circles take the coastal area from about 4,800 to about 12,400 km2 (ratio 2.6), the researcher's reading of the tripling; the page names no place gained. The islands (Rab, Hvar, Korčula, Pag, Brač, Cres, Krk) are kept throughout (Stato da Màr dates). [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: islands added]

Morean War: "the fortress of Sinj finally fell to the Venetian army on 30 September 1686." The islands (Rab, Hvar, Korčula, Pag, Brač, Cres, Krk) are kept throughout (Stato da Màr dates). [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: islands added]

keyframe_review.note: Morean War: the siege of Castelnuovo ended with a Venetian victory in September 1687 (the page gives 30 and 31 September). The islands (Rab, Hvar, Korčula, Pag, Brač, Cres, Krk) are kept throughout (Stato da Màr dates). [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: islands added]

correction.text: after Karlowitz: "Venice did relinquish the areas of Popovo polje as well as Klek and Sutorina"; the Dalmatian coast, islands and hinterland within Croatia, the Bay of Kotor side and, to 1718, Čitluk and Gabela

keyframe_review.note: Morean War, 26 January 1699. The circles removed (17.8 E, 42.88 N and 18.5 E, 42.46 N) are the researcher's reading of Popovo polje, Klek and Sutorina. From 1699 the hinterland circles are intersected with Croatia, because the Dalmatia-Bosnia border fixed at Karlowitz is today's (Morean War page: Knin "helped set the Dalmatia-Bosnia border that exists today"); the Bay of Kotor side (Kotor, Budva, Herceg Novi without Sutorina, which went to the Ottomans) is added; the strip round Čitluk and Gabela (17.7 E, 43.1 N, 20 km) stays Venetian until 1718 (Venetian Dalmatia: "Čitluk and Gabela were lost to the Ottomans" by the Treaty of Passarowitz). The earlier shape put 19 cells of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Venetian hands. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: clipped to Croatia]

correction.text: after Passarowitz: Sinj and Imotski gained, Čitluk and Gabela lost; Croatia's Dalmatia, the islands and the Bay of Kotor side

keyframe_review.note: Venetian Dalmatia: "Sebastiano Mocenigo gained Sinj and Imotski, the last Venetian enlargement. Čitluk and Gabela were lost to the Ottomans." The Albania Veneta page adds that in 1718-1797 Venice "extended its territory south toward the Republic of Ragusa while keeping the Kotor and Budva enclaves"; that extension is not drawn. From 1718 Čitluk and Gabela are out, and the hinterland (Sinj, Knin, Vrgorac, the Neretva delta and Imotski) is limited to Croatia; no cell of Bosnia and Herzegovina remains. About 52 cells (about 13,156 km2). [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: clipped to Croatia]

wars.name: Venetian conquest of Dalmatia against Sigismund
wars.outcome: Venice bought Ladislaus's rights in 1409, beat Sigismund's forces at Motta in 1412 and held the coastal cities by 1420, except Ragusa.
wars.note: The war name is the researcher's: the page gives no name.

wars.name: Candia War
wars.outcome: The Ottomans took Krk, Pag, Cres and Novigrad in 1646; the peace of 1669 left Venice's territory roughly tripled.

wars.name: Morean War

zones.text: Sinj, Knin, Vrgorac and the land north of Ragusa

wars.outcome: Venice took Sinj (1686), Herceg Novi (1687), Knin (1688), Vrgorac (1690) and the land north of Ragusa (1694); at Karlowitz (26 January 1699) it gave up Popovo polje, Klek and Sutorina.

wars.name: Second Morean War (Ottoman-Venetian war of 1714-1718)
wars.outcome: The Ottomans reclaimed the Morea in 1715; in 1718 Venice gained Sinj and Imotski and lost Čitluk and Gabela.
wars.note: The Morean War page says the Ottomans "reversed Venice's gains" in 1718; neither page gives the war's start year, which is taken from the 1715 campaign.

certainty.note: Coastal cities and islands with hinterlands as the Ottoman front moved; no surveyed line on the pages opened.

The Dalmatia-Bosnia border was fixed by Karlowitz (1699) and adjusted at Passarowitz (1718); the page says Knin 1688 "helped set the Dalmatia-Bosnia border that exists today". The Kotor and Budva enclaves are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria has no row; all ten keyframes are new and rest on city-radius circles because the pages give no map or area. Venetian Albania is only partly covered: Kotor and Budva are included from 1420; Durrës (to 1501), Shkodër (to 1479), Lezhë, Ulcinj and Bar (to 1571/1573) belong to a separate Albania Veneta dossier (not written; the Albania Veneta page is silent on their dates) and the 1573 move of the southern limit to Kufin near Budva is not in the ledger. Disagreements: Venetian Dalmatia page has Sinj and Imotski gained in 1718, the Morean War page has Sinj fallen on 30 September 1686; Herceg Novi surrendered on 30 or 31 September 1687 (the Morean page). The Venetian Dalmatia page says the Ottomans took Krk and Cres in 1646, which is unusual and unconfirmed by a second page. The Venetian Dalmatia page names no Cyprus War (1570-1573) change, the Treaty of Karlowitz or Passarowitz by name for Dalmatia, and no Provveditore dates. Wikidata id null (unreachable). Counterparts needing dossiers: albania-veneta; Kotor and Budva communes before 1420. Review fix (2026-11-01): (1) The islands are now drawn from the Stato da Màr page (Rab, Hvar, Korčula 1409; Pag, Brač 1420; Krk 1480; Cres with Lošinj '15C', bridged to 1420 at confidence 1); Brač, Hvar and Korčula are on that page, not on the Venetian Dalmatia page, which the reviewer's list of islands lacked a page for. Lošinj, Vis and the small islands are inside the circles or not drawn. (2) The 1646 loss (Novigrad, Krk, Pag, Cres) is drawn for 1646 only and reversed in 1647: Novigrad's return is the Venetian Dalmatia page's ("the following year"), the islands' return is a bridge at confidence 1 because neither page dates it. (3) From 1699 the hinterland is clipped to Croatia and the Bay of Kotor side (Kotor, Budva, Herceg Novi without the Sutorina circle) is added, as the reviewer asked, EXCEPT that the Čitluk and Gabela strip (17.7 E, 43.1 N, 20 km) is kept in the 1699-1717 shape because the page says it was lost in 1718, so Venice held it; the reviewer's literal instruction (Croatia only) would have made the 1718 loss an event with nothing to remove. The strip is 4 cells of Bosnia and Herzegovina; bosnia-eyalet subtracts it for 1699-1717. (4) Counterparts of the 1669 and 1686-1694 gains and of the 1699 and 1718 losses are bosnia-eyalet. (5) The first Candia War overlap: the 55 km Split circle already contains Sinj, so the 1686 Sinj gain adds no cell; the circles remain the researcher's reading. Sutorina (Montenegro) is subtracted from the Herceg Novi municipality in 1699-1796 and is not drawn for the Ottoman side either; Klek and Popovo polje are Bosnian cells of bosnia-eyalet.
